judged_text: The fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no timeout/AbortSignal, making it a timeout-less outbound call on the token-refresh path which executes inside user-facing booking and calendar operations. A hung or slow sync endpoint stalls each affected calendar operation for the platform's default connect/idle timeouts (undici: minutes), piling up concurrent booking requests and worker capacity on a dependency that is not on any critical provider's SLA.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the code calls `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams(...) })` with no `AbortSignal`/timeout handling. This new network dependency is then used on token refresh paths (e.g., Google/Office365/Zoom/Webex/etc. services now call `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`), so a slow/hung sync endpoint can stall those operations. The diff does not implement any timeout/cancellation, so the concern is diff-grounded, but it’s primarily a resilience/availability issue rather than a deterministic functional correctness defect.
